LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.2: Phonological

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Phonological
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What produces the 3 lessons of single-syllable words my home, individually, in pairs sounds we hear?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. add or substitute individual sounds them(depends on each languag
2. recognise and sound the  Learners participate in language commonly used letter sounds and games e.g. guess- the word game, syllables change- a name game as they

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Phonological

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Phonological

Teach
• Focus skill: add or substitute individual sounds them(depends on each languag.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Phonological.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Phonological
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What produces the 3 lessons of single-syllable words my home, individually, in pairs sounds we hear?
2. How do we say and onset rimes of single-syllable produce initial, middle and final those sounds?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
